Paragraph:
Translation: Thus far I have declared to you the analytical knowledge of sankhya philosophy. Now listen to the knowledge of yoga whereby one works without fruitive result. O son of Prtha, when you act by such intelligence, you can free yourself from the bondage of works.

Purport (Excerpt): ...sankhya refers to that philosophy which describes the real nature of the soul. And yoga involves controlling the senses... Consequently, Krsna will now tell him about the working process in buddhi-yoga, or karma-yoga, or in other words, the practice of devotional service only for the sense gratification of the Lord... One who works for the satisfaction of the Lord only, however difficult such work may be, is working under the principles of buddhi-yoga and finds himself always in transcendental bliss.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Arjuna has received theoretical knowledge (Sankhya) about the immortal soul, but needs to know how to practically apply this in the messy, active world without getting entangled.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna transitions from theory (Sankhya/analytical knowledge) to practice (Buddhi-yoga/Karma-yoga). He promises to teach the practical application of working with intelligence that frees one from the bondage of material actions.
Outcome/Resolution: A shift occurs from passive philosophy to active, spiritualized engagement in the world.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Integration of Theory and Practice: Moving from knowing what is right to actually doing it
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Mindful Action: Working with higher awareness and purpose
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Cognitive Reframing of Work: Changing the internal motivation for daily tasks

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Sankhya (Analytical study of matter and spirit)
Buddhi-yoga (The yoga of intelligence; working without attachment to fruitive results; devotional service)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Krishna marks a clear transition in his teaching. He moves from the analytical study of the soul (Sankhya) to the practical science of acting in consciousness of the Supreme (Buddhi-yoga). Working with this transcendental intelligence severs the chains of karma, transforming mundane work into liberating spiritual practice.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Theoretical knowledge alone rarely cures psychological distress. You can intellectually know you shouldn't worry (Sankhya), but still feel anxiety. Krishna introduces the 'yoga'—the practical, behavioral steps. By aligning one's intelligence (Buddhi) with a higher purpose and acting without selfish motives, an individual breaks free from the exhausting 'bondage' of always striving for personal validation and material results.
